we have successfully implemented a concept for HiL testing of PLC applications using an extension of Structured Text.
the proposed concept for PLC HiL testing is able to: • Use IEC 61130-3 programming languages to specify HiL test cases.
we developed an extension for structured text that enables HiL test specification and we evaluated the usability and feasibility of this extension by a survey.

the following questions: (i) What are the challenges and requirements for HiL test specification?
the following aspects: (1) the definition of a new HiL testing language, (2) the implementation of a test specification language interpreter and (3) the implementation of the HiL test environment.

the following aspects: (1) The development of a HiL test specification language, which is an extension of structured test, (2) a HiL tool that is able to execute test cases specified in the new language and (3) the evaluation of the new language and tool.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed concept of HiL simulation is a promising and feasible approach to reduce the complexity and the effort of PLC HiL testing.
the presented approach allows to use a programming language specified by IEC61131-3 as a specification language for hardware-in-the-loop tests.
the proposed method allows the user to write HiL test specifications in the programming language he or she is already familiar with.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a concept to test PLCs with the help of a programming language.

we present a concept to use IEC 61130-3 programming languages for HiL test specification and we show that it is possible to implement this concept in an existing HiL tool, which is the basis for future research.
the presented approach is a concept of HiL test case specification in the domain of structured text.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the test specification language is not a barrier to HiL testing.
the test cases are specified using structured text (ST) and the resulting test cases are executed by an interpreter that is integrated into the HiL simulation.
HiL tests can be specified in a programming language that is familiar to PLC programmers, and that the resulting test code is portable to different HiL tools.
